title: Account Executive - Virtual Data Rooms (North America)
description:

DoneDiligence pairs a secure, scalable VDR with AI built into every room. Buyer questions get answered directly from the documents. New uploads are indexed automatically. Missing or inconsistent items surface before they hit the Q&A queue. Teasers and CIMs are drafted from the source material in a fraction of the manual time.
We are building the next generation of deal execution infrastructure, where valuation, data rooms, and AI-powered analysis come together in one seamless workflow.
The Opportunity:
We are hiring an experienced Account Executive with deep experience selling Virtual Data Rooms or adjacent M&A deal execution platforms. You will own the full sales cycle for DoneDiligence into M&A advisors, private equity, investment banks, and corporate development teams.
Your Responsibilities:

• Own the full sales cycle from prospecting to close

• Outreach via calls, email, LinkedIn, and account-based strategies

• Lead qualification, discovery, product demonstrations, negotiation, and closing

• Sell Valutico ’s Due Diligence Suite, including:

• Secure and scalable Virtual Data Room (VDR)

• AI-powered due diligence assistant

• Integrated valuation and analysis capabilities

• Engage senior stakeholders across:

• Private Equity & Venture Capital

• M&A advisory and investment banking

• Corporate finance and corporate development teams

• Audit, tax advisory, and consulting firms

• Clearly communicate complex product value in high-trust, high-stakes deal environments

• Contribute to and help refine global go-to-market strategy for the Due Diligence product line

• After onboarding (3-6 months), take ownership of an SDR to support pipeline generation and meeting booking

Requirements
What We’re Looking For:

• 5+ years of experience in B2B SaaS sales, with at least 2+ years selling VDRs, due diligence platforms, or M&A workflow software (Datasite, Ansarada, Intralinks, iDeals, Drooms, FirmRoom, SecureDocs, DealRoom, or similar)

• Existing network in the M&A advisor, private equity, investment banking, or corporate development communities is a strong plus

• Strong commercial instincts and ability to navigate long, structured sales cycles

• Experience engaging senior stakeholders such as Partners, Directors, Investment Professionals, or Corporate Development teams

• Self-direction in a remote, international, fast-moving environment.

• Excellent communication skills and the ability to build trust in high-stakes environments

Benefits
What We Offer:

• A high-growth, international, remote-first environment

• A category-expanding product at the intersection of VDR, AI, and financial workflows

• Strong sales leadership, structured onboarding, and a performance-driven culture

• Modern, data-driven sales stack with automation-first tooling

• Above-market, uncapped commission structure

• Clear expectations, transparent targets, and a strong track record of high performance across the team

• Real ownership in shaping how a next-generation Due Diligence platform is sold globally

Why This Role Is Different:
You are not just selling a Virtual Data Room.
You are selling a next-generation deal execution platform that combines:

• Secure data rooms

• AI native due diligence

• Integrated valuation and financial analysis tools

This is an opportunity to move beyond traditional VDR sales and help redefine how deals are executed globally.

title: Implementation Manager, Commercial
description:
About Engine

Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020-2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

As an  Implementation Manager at Engine, you'll own the onboarding experience for some of our most important new customers, setting them up for long-term success on the platform. You'll craft tailored rollout plans, drive product adoption across our full suite, and partner closely with Sales and Account Management to deliver a smooth handoff into the customer lifecycle. This is a high-impact role where innovation meets collaboration, and where the work you do directly shapes how quickly and deeply new customers embrace Engine.

Note: this role requires that you work 3 days/week from our Chicago office at 500 W Madison St, Chicago, IL 60661  

Your Mission:

• Design and execute onboarding strategies for Engine's new customer opportunities (deals ranging from $200K to $1M), setting the foundation for lasting partnerships.

• Drive product adoption across Engine's full suite during a customer's first months on the platform.

• Partner with Sales and Account Management to unlock new opportunities and deliver a seamless customer experience from signed contract to first booking.

• Lead implementation and onboarding processes that scale efficiently, driving adoption in the first year and preparing customers for a smooth transition to their dedicated Account Manager.

• Serve as a trusted advisor to customers by leading key meetings, delivering training, and ensuring every interaction with Engine exceeds expectations.

What You’ll Bring to Engine: 

• Minimum 3 years of experience in sales, account management, customer success, or implementation

• Subject matter expertise in onboarding and customer success, with a track record of thriving in fast-paced, innovative environments

• A problem-solver's mindset. You anticipate customer needs, remove friction, and build conviction through consultative conversations.

• Comfort owning ambitious performance goals, including high win rates through onboarding milestones, meeting weekly customer engagement targets (roughly 15 customer meetings per week), and hitting adoption benchmarks in the first six months of a customer's lifecycle

• Strong cross-functional skills across Sales, Account Management, and customer-facing teams

• Bonus points if you're fluent in building configuration and rollout plans, drafting mutual success plans, and coordinating handoffs across GTM teams

Applications for this role will be accepted through November 6, 2026 or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

title: Data Engineer
description:

Product Strategy. Technology Execution. Launch. Investment.

Remedy Product Studio is a rapidly scaling technology company specializing in working with and investing in prominent start-ups and brands in building and scaling their digital products. We use data-driven agile approaches coupled with high performing teams as a cornerstone of our technology-first culture.
We partner with startups to strategize, execute, launch, and invest in digital products, including web apps, mobile apps, data science tools, and firmware for connected devices.
We believe that people make a great company, and that's why we want you to join us!!!

As a Senior Data Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining scalable data pipelines and storage solutions. You will work closely with product managers, engineers, and analysts to ensure efficient data workflows and enable data-driven decision-making. • Design, develop, and maintain scalable ETL/ELT pipelines and data workflows.

• Optimize data storage, processing, and retrieval using cloud-based technologies, with a strong focus on AWS.

• Ensure data integrity, security, and compliance with industry standards.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define data requirements and support analytics and machine learning initiatives.

• Monitor and improve data infrastructure performance, ensuring reliability and scalability.

• Implement best practices for data governance, quality, and observability.

• Develop and maintain robust data injection processes to ensure seamless data flow across systems.

• Design and optimize data models to support analytical and operational use cases.

What should your qualifications be

• 5+ years of experience in data engineering or a related field.

• Strong expertise in AWS data services (e.g., Redshift, Glue, Athena, S3, Lambda, Kinesis, etc.).

• Strong hands-on experience in Python

• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

• Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Fluent English (B2) with both written and spoken skills used for clear and active communication with native speakers
Nice to Have:

• Experience with real-time data streaming and event-driven architectures.

• Exposure to machine learning workflows and MLOps practices.

• Knowledge of security and compliance standards in data engineering.

• Experience with GCP or Azure is a plus (BigQuery, Databricks, Azure Data Factory, etc.)

title: TAN RIA Product Shelf Manager
description:
The TAN RIA Product Shelf Manager is responsible for managing, governing, and optimizing the Thrivent Advisor Network (TAN) investment advisory product shelf. This role serves as the primary point of contact for advisors, firm CIOs, and internal stakeholders regarding investment solutions, product availability, and new product requests. The position coordinates product evaluations, due diligence activities, governance processes, and product implementation efforts to ensure the advisory platform remains competitive and aligned with advisor and client needs. This role requires advanced investment knowledge across managed accounts, third-party managers, alternatives, model portfolios, and specialized investment solutions. The Product Shelf Manager works cross-functionally with Due Diligence, Compliance, Legal, Operations, Technology, and Distribution partners to deliver a high-quality advisory product offering. This role reports to the Complex Investment Solutions Manager.

This can be a remote position within the United States. DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Maintains overall ownership and governance of the TAN investment advisory product shelf, including product availability, manager rosters, documentation, and ongoing maintenance. 

• Serves as the primary intake point for advisors, firm CIO, and business requests related to new investment solutions, managers, platforms, and product capabilities. 

• Coordinates initial and ongoing due diligence reviews with internal due diligence teams and external research providers; facilitates review and decision-making processes but does not perform investment due diligence. 

• Evaluates product shelf gaps, redundancies, and enhancement opportunities, making recommendations to improve competitiveness, advisor adoption, and client outcomes. 

• Leads evaluation and coordination of complex product requests, including SMAs, UMAs, alternatives, exchange funds, options-based strategies, private market solutions, and other specialized investment offerings. 

• Acts as a trusted resource to TAN firm CIOs, advisors, and internal stakeholders regarding product capabilities, eligibility requirements, implementation considerations, and appropriate use cases. 

• Partners with Compliance, Legal, Risk, Operations, and Technology teams to facilitate product approval, implementation, governance, and ongoing oversight. 

• Monitors industry trends, competitive platforms, emerging investment solutions, and advisor demand to proactively identify product enhancement opportunities. 

• Represents the advisory product shelf and business requirements on strategic initiatives, platform enhancement efforts, and cross-functional projects. 

• Works collaboratively with Distribution, Product Management, and Wealth Management leadership to ensure alignment with enterprise strategy and advisor needs. 

• Models Thrivent’s leadership competencies: Model the Way, Rally the Team, and Deliver Outcomes. 

• Supports and/or develops an environment in which Thrivent employees and colleagues are focused on continuous improvement, exceptional employee engagement, and an unwavering commitment to advisors and clients. Shapes and/or supports a culture that represents the Thrivent purpose, promise, and values, ensuring that Thrivent’s trust and reputation remain strong.

Audience & Interaction / Influence  
TIMI Due Diligence Teams : Coordinate product reviews, manager approvals, and ongoing monitoring activities.

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril’s Manufacturing Safety Engineering team partners across Anduril’s manufacturing, engineering, and operations organizations to ensure our production systems are safe to build, test, and sustain at scale. As an engineering discipline, we design safety into the way products are made, covering the equipment, fixtures, test stations, and work instructions on the factory floor, rather than inspecting for it after the fact. Our mandate spans the production lifecycle, from new equipment and line design through ramp and sustained operations. We apply formal risk assessment and the hierarchy of controls to identify hazards early and engineer them out, partnering closely with our Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) experts, controls and manufacturing engineers, and production leadership to keep our people safe while moving at the speed Anduril demands.

ABOUT THE JOB
We are seeking an experienced Manufacturing Safety Engineering leader to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA to stand up and scale manufacturing safety as an engineering discipline across Anduril. This is a build role: you will create the manufacturing-safety-engineering team, define the risk-assessment framework and processes that keep our production equipment, fixtures, test stations, and work instructions safe, and drive adoption of those practices across Anduril’s manufacturing sites. As a Manufacturing Safety leader, you will apply deep expertise in machine safety, formal risk assessment, and the hierarchy of controls to engineer hazards out of how our products are built, partnering closely with EHS, manufacturing and controls engineering, and production leadership. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technical leader who can set strategy and standards while remaining the senior authority on the hardest hazard problems on the floor.
This role is based in Costa Mesa, CA, and supports Anduril’s manufacturing operations, including sites at Quonset Point, RI and Atlanta, GA; travel to production sites is expected.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Build, lead, and develop the Manufacturing Safety Engineering team, including hiring, leveling, mentoring, and performance management, as the discipline scales across Anduril.

• Establish and standardize the manufacturing-safety framework: risk-assessment methodology, templates, risk-acceptance criteria, safety sign-off gates, and the management-of-change process, aligned to the business.

• Grow the manufacturing-safety discipline across Anduril, driving adoption across production lines and sites and defining the standards of record, in partnership with Manufacturing, EHS, and product engineering.

• Define and communicate the discipline’s vision, goals, roadmap, and operating model, and integrate manufacturing-safety practices across all stages of production development.

• Own manufacturing-safety metrics, KPIs, and executive-level reporting; represent the discipline to leadership and to customer and defense-program stakeholders.

Organic search is one of Airbnb's largest and most efficient acquisition channels, and the rise of AI answer engines is reshaping how travelers discover places to stay, things to do, and trusted Hosts. As Senior Growth Marketing Lead, SEO, AEO, GEO, you will own the strategy and day-to-day execution for how Airbnb shows up in Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and the assistants that come next. • Build and evolve the measurement framework for SEO, AEO, and GEO - attribution models, leading and lagging indicators, dashboards, and revenue impact - including the ability to demonstrate the value of work that's difficult to attribute, such as preventive technical work or emerging AI channels.

title: Staff Product Manager, Agent Connectivity
description:
ROLE SUMMARY

We're at an inflection point. We started with core durable execution and are now evolving with the world as it transitions to AI. What it takes to get from where we are today to a world where Temporal underpins all software - including and especially agents - is going to be different. It will require unprecedented speed, iteration, market and customer focus, and invention.

As an Agent Connectivity PM, you’ll help the world makes its transition to AI on Temporal. Without any effort, the market has already identified Temporal as a good substrate for agent workloads. But what makes agents powerful is connecting them to services and data. We are in the infancy of building out our connectivity layer, called Nexus, which has been the brainchild of our founder, Maxim, for many years. We now need to realize the full vision of Nexus by continuing to build out foundational capabilities like xyz and importantly, building agent-specific features and integrations, e.g., MCP connector, tool registry. You’ll identify the highest leverage areas for us to invest, and work closely with the founder/CTO and engineering team to get them to market.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Deeply understand problems faced by agent builders and identify opportunities where our products can make building agents faster, more intuitive, more reliable, and more powerful.

- Define and build what’s next for Temporal. Own strategy and roadmap for agent connectivity. Turn ambiguous signals into clear product theses. How should we prioritize new capabilities like identity propagation or rate limits? How do we bootstrap an ecosystem of connectors?

- Perform up-front discovery and translate customer, field, and open-source community signals into small tweaks, brand new abstractions, or platform bets.

- Help engineers and designers deeply understand user needs, empowering them to make great product decisions.

- Craft messaging around upcoming features that resonates with users.

- Enable sales and marketing teams to effectively communicate with and win customers.

- Strong technical depth. Ability to reason about distributed systems, workflow orchestration, service-to-service communication, APIs, SDKs, identity, and authorization.

- Developer-platform experience. Experience with infrastructure, platforms, integrations, APIs, SDKs, service mesh, API gateways, or cloud developer products.

You’ll build new things with a massive tailwind behind you: a proven technology, a large and growing customer base, and a market moving toward problems Temporal is uniquely equipped to solve. The opportunity is to turn that momentum into what comes next-not simply scale what already works. You’ll be expected to move fast, work across boundaries, and do what it takes to make it happen.

WHO YOU ARE

- You're ambitious. You want to win big. You don’t need someone else to set the pace. You get impatient when good ideas stay in slide decks, Slack, or meetings.

- You're an owner. You are accountable to results over the process. You’re less focused on your swim lane and more focused on making the company successful. You have exceptional product and operational judgement.

- You're resilient. Building at a high-growth company in 2026 is not for the faint of heart. You see the challenges and change as not just normal, but actually desirable.

- You want to grow, and help others grow. You self-reflect often. You give feedback, and you seek it out. You have shameless curiosity and a propensity to question things deeply.

- You prioritize the customer above all else. You want to understand our users' world and prioritize solving their problems above everything else.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

- You have 8+ years of product management experience

- You have technical depth, with experience working on platform, infrastructure, developer tools, or other technical products

- You have worked at a startup, high-growth company or in a similarly intense and ambiguous environment

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

- Nexus

title: Consultant - Child Rights
description:
ChildFund Australia is a member of the ChildFund Alliance - a global network of 10 organisations which assists almost 36 million children and their families in 66 countries. ChildFund Australia directly manages and implements programs with a range of local partners in Cambodia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste, Vietnam, and other Pacific nations, and manages projects delivered by partner organisations throughout Asia, Africa, and the Americas.
Purpose
ChildFund seeks to strengthen its existing participation approach so that stakeholders can engage with, validate, challenge, and enrich the findings of Child Rights Situation Analyses, helping to identify priority issues, emerging trends, evidence gaps, and opportunities for action. The resulting insights will inform organisational strategy, country planning, program portfolios, advocacy priorities, and investment decisions, ensuring that these are grounded not only in published evidence but also in the perspectives and experiences of children and communities themselves.
This assignment will develop practical guidelines, tools, and supporting resources that enable this process to be undertaken consistently across country contexts. The approach should be low burden, repeatable, and designed to leverage existing community engagement structures wherever possible, recognising the capacity constraints facing Country Offices and partners. It should also promote accountability by establishing clear mechanisms for reporting back on how participant feedback influenced findings, priorities, and subsequent decisions.
The consultant will also provide technical advice on the role of Youth Voice in ChildFund’s strategy development and broader strategic decision-making, including its evolving purpose, Terms of Reference, engagement processes and feedback mechanisms.
The consultancy period is 20 days spread across 3 months.
Interested consultants should submit an expression of interest including: a technical proposal (max. 3 pages) outlining understanding of the assignment, proposed search strategy and sources, and workplan; a financial proposal/fee schedule in USD; a curriculum vitae including at least two references from similar assignments; and a sample of previous, similar written work.
ChildFund Australia believes in a global community where children are safe and can reach their full potential. We take extensive steps to safeguard children in any work done by our people, i.e., our staff, volunteers and interns, supporters, partners, board members, ambassadors and suppliers. We strive to keep children safe through child safe practices, and rigorously ensure we prevent, oppose, and combat all exploitation and abuse of children and vulnerable people. As part of this commitment, all people working with us will undergo relevant background checks before joining ChildFund Australia .
At ChildFund Australia , all staff must remain alert and responsive to any child safeguarding or sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment (SEAH) risks. Staff will acquire the knowledge and skills needed to understand our Child Safeguarding and PSEAH policies & procedures, promote strong safeguarding practices, and conduct themselves consistent with these policies.
In line with our values, diversity of people and ideas is critical to our work and our success at ChildFund Australia . We strive for a team culture that is welcoming, inclusive, and supportive. ChildFund is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer and strongly encourages people from all backgrounds, abilities, and identities to apply

title: Senior Database Administrator (Freelancer)
description:
Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. Most modernization work doesn't ship, it stalls in pilots, slips a year, or lands at three times the budget. We exist to ship it: production systems running, legacy retired, outcomes measured. Our delivery is built on Aedeon, the agent platform built by Mactores ' founders' sister company, which absorbs the repetitive 60-70% of engagement work, discovery, dependency mapping, validation, test generation, that traditional consulting bills human hours against. Forward-deployed engineers own the rest: architecture, judgment, and cutover, on dates we commit to in the contract.
Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migrations don't fail at conversion. They fail at go-live DMS latency nobody diagnosed, autovacuum behavior nobody tuned, privilege mappings nobody tested, incidents nobody owns at 2 a.m. This role sits inside our Application & Database Modernization pillar and exists to make sure that doesn't happen.
As our Senior Database Administrator, you'll run the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL environments in an active Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration program from cluster design through DMS replication through post-go-live stabilization. Aedeon handles the repeatable conversion and validation work; you own what agents can't: production judgment. When replication lags, when a workload misbehaves after cutover, when an incident escalates past L2, you're the person who resolves it and can explain why it happened.
This is a freelance engagement, remote, working as the L3 escalation point on production systems that real businesses run on.
What you will do?

• Design, set up, configure, and manage Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters.

• Configure parameters, maintenance windows, monitoring, and scaling strategies.

• Keep the environments highly available, fault tolerant, and operationally ready - before go-live, not after.

• Map users, roles, and privileges from Oracle to PostgreSQL.

• Implement least-privilege access, role hierarchies, and security best practices, and support audit and compliance requirements.

• Configure, run, monitor, and optimize AWS DMS tasks (Full Load and CDC).

• Troubleshoot DMS latency, data mismatches, and performance issues, and tune DMS settings for large-volume, high-throughput workloads.

• Tune server and database performance - CPU, memory, I/O, connections - plus PostgreSQL parameters, autovacuum, indexing, and query behavior.

• Find performance bottlenecks before the customer does, and resolve them.

• Design and implement backup and restore strategies; define and test DR and failover procedures; support cross-region replication and recovery drills.

• Lead post-go-live stabilization: monitor production workloads, resolve incidents, and act as the L3 escalation point for database-related production issues.

• Deliver operational documentation and handover support, so what you stabilized stays stable after you.

What are we looking for?

• 5+ years of experience administering Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.

• Proven expertise supporting Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migrations.

• Hands-on experience with AWS DMS.

• Advanced PostgreSQL performance tuning and troubleshooting skills.

• Strong knowledge of backup, restore, and DR planning in AWS.

• Experience with AWS monitoring tools (CloudWatch, Performance Insights).

• Strong problem-solving and root-cause analysis abilities.

• Experience working in production and post-go-live environments.

• The ability to work independently as an L3 escalation engineer.

• Clear communication and documentation skills.

You will be preferred if

• Familiarity with automation and configuration management tools, such as Ansible, Chef, or Puppet

• Familiarity with IAAC tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation

• Familiarity with CI/CD implementation tools like Liquibase/Flyway

• AWS Certified Database - Specialty

• AWS Certified Solutions Architect

How we work?
We refactor legacy databases to cloud-native AWS on a committed date, with Mactores car

title: Growth Strategist
description:
GROWTH STRATEGIST

At Fresh Prints , we work with thousands of customers, but not every customer should have the same experience with us.

Some might be ordering for the first time. Others have been buying from us for years. Some need an occasional reminder or a well-timed offer, while others represent significant opportunities that deserve a much more personalized approach.

Today, we reach these customers through emails, SMS, automated journeys, promotional campaigns, gifting programs, and direct outreach. We've built much of the infrastructure to make these things possible, but there's a much bigger opportunity ahead of us: bringing all of these touchpoints together into a thoughtful, cohesive strategy for how we grow our customer relationships.

That's what we're hiring a Growth Strategist to do.

Your job is to understand our customers, figure out what they need at different stages of their relationship with Fresh Prints , and build experiences that make them want to engage, purchase, return, and grow with us.

For some customers, that might mean a great email at exactly the right moment. For others, it might mean an entirely different experience, with personalized outreach, exclusive offers, samples, or programs designed around their long-term potential.

We don't want someone who thinks about growth as a collection of campaigns or channels. We want someone who can see the bigger picture, identify where the opportunities are, and turn those opportunities into programs that drive meaningful business results.

This isn't a role where you inherit a finished playbook. You'll have the freedom, and responsibility, to question how we do things today, build better systems, and shape what customer growth looks like at Fresh Prints .

This role is about:

•
Understanding our customers deeply: Who they are, what they care about, why they buy, what brings them back, and what makes them disengage.

•
Designing the right experience for different customers: Knowing when automation and great content are enough, and when a relationship deserves a more personalized, high-touch approach.

•
Finding opportunities to grow customer value: Identifying where we're losing customers, leaving revenue on the table, or missing opportunities to build stronger relationships.

•
Being a great marketer: Understanding what makes someone open an email, click a link, respond to an offer, or take the next step, and being able to create that experience yourself.

•
Turning ideas into execution: Building programs, writing compelling content, coordinating teams, testing approaches, and taking ownership of the results.

•
Building systems that scale: Using data, technology, AI, and automation to create experiences that become smarter and more effective over time.

What You'll Own

Understanding Customers & Finding Growth Opportunities

• Develop a deep understanding of Fresh Prints ' customers, their buying behavior, motivations, needs, and decision-making journeys.

• Use customer insights, data, and commercial judgment to identify the biggest opportunities to improve engagement, conversion, repeat purchases, retention, and customer value.

• Build meaningful customer segments based on behavior, lifecycle stage, value, and growth potential, rather than treating everyone on our list the same way.

• Identify where different customers need different experiences, and determine where we should invest more time, effort, and resources.

• Continuously question our existing approach and develop new ideas that could materially change how customers engage and grow with Fresh Prints .

Building Experiences That Drive Growth

• Own how Fresh Prints engages with customers throughout their relationship with us, from their first interaction to becoming loyal, repeat customers.

• Develop thoughtful customer journeys that bring together content, communication, offers, personalization, and outreach to move customers toward the next meaningful action.

• Own the strategy, mess

title: Senior Google Ads Buyer, DTC eCommerce
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.

•
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.

title: Associate Director of Assessment Development

NCBE is committed to fostering a collaborative, mission-driven environment with competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, flexible scheduling, and professional development opportunities. NCBE’s headquarters is based in Madison, Wisconsin, a dynamic community with exceptional amenities.
The Associate Director of Assessment Development oversees the creation of content and the construction of assessment forms for one or more of NCBE’s assessment programs, with a main focus on the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination. The associate director may manage staff editors who work with subject matter experts to draft items, select items for use on assessment forms, and create other related materials, including for grading, study aids and licensing, marketing, and training. This person works closely with the Director of Assessment Development and the psychometric team to ensure that the items and assessments achieve appropriate levels of quality in terms of fairness, reliability, and validity. The associate director also works closely with many departments including operations (printing, publishing, accessibility, and administration), IT (item banking, delivery), and psychometrics (design, scoring, analysis and reporting). This role serves as a key resource on content matters to NCBE stakeholders, both internally and externally, on the program. The associate director is specialized in a measurement component (e.g., selected response doctrinal measurement, performance assessments, integrated assessments) aligned with the program they oversee.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

• Works with psychometric staff to ensure that NCBE’s assessments are in compliance with professional standards for educational testing.

• Oversees development of assessment content including items, forms, grading material, study aids, technical documentation, and other materials.

• Advises on measurement specialization across programs and contributes expertise as required.

• Assists with recruitment of subject matter experts and ensures appropriate training, including for drafting and review committees.

• Collaborates with the operations team on the development of production schedules, implementation of security procedures for assessment materials, and appropriate staff/resource allocation to ensure efficient, high-quality services, problem resolution, and on-time delivery of materials.

• Ensures adherence to existing NCBE policies and procedures, updates as needed, and manages policies and procedures that meet the highest standards of quality, security, accuracy, and efficiency for content development and construction of assessments.

• Encourages process improvement by staff and promotes a mindset that fosters continuous quality improvement.

• Participates in research and contributes to the design and development of new NCBE programs, processes, products, or services.

• Assists with inquiries or complaints regarding assessment content.

• May manage staff in the day-to-day performance of their jobs.

• Develops and provides presentations for meetings, conferences, workshops, and seminars.

• Travel to committee meetings or conferences is expected.

Qualifications:

• Graduate of an ABA-approved law school and admitted to the bar in at least one jurisdiction.

• At least 10 years of significant professional legal experience with a demonstrated knowledge of professional responsibility law and a willingness to develop additional expertise in the relevant subject-matter.

• Ability to develop working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including subject matter experts.

• Proficiency in MS Word

title: Manager, Developer Advocacy (EMEA)

We’re looking for someone to run Developer Advocacy in EMEA. You’ll get to shape how developers across the region first find Temporal, and you’ll also see it through to the other end, helping our biggest customers build serious systems on it.

You’ll manage a team of advocates, but this isn’t a desk job. You’ll still give talks, run workshops, write code, and sit down with customers yourself. If it’s been a while since you built a demo from scratch, this probably isn’t the right fit.

EMEA covers a lot of ground. The UK, Germany, France, the Netherlands, and the Nordics have big developer communities and some of our largest customers.

You’ll spend a lot of time with our Marketing department on events and community, and with Sales, Solutions Architects, and Developer Success on customer accounts. Good relationships with all of them are your key to success.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Hire, coach, and support a team of Developer Advocates spread across the region. Set priorities, then trust them to adapt to their own markets and audiences.

- Decide how the team splits its time between community and customer work. Sort incoming customer requests by deal size, stage, and strategic value, and make the tough calls when there’s more demand than people, without letting community work get pushed aside.

- Find the people in local communities who care about the problems Temporal solves and help them lead, contribute to open source, and spread the word.

- People leadership experience or a clear readiness to step into it; you can coach senior individual contributors while still doing the work yourself.

- Strong hands-on technical credibility: you can build, demo, and teach, and earn the respect of senior enterprise engineers.

- An operational, execution-first mindset: you can run a repeatable program, manage intake and prioritization, and keep commitments against an SLA.

- Comfort working cross-functionally with Sales, SAs, Dev Success, Product, and Marketing, and translating technical engagement into commercial impact.

- Experience operating across a linguistically and culturally diverse region and coordinating a distributed team across multiple time zones; additional European languages are a plus.

- A genuine passion for empowering developers and creating authentic, high-trust community experiences, not sales pitches.

- Familiarity with durable execution, workflow orchestration, or distributed systems (e.g., Temporal) is a strong plus.

- Hands-on experience building on multiple cloud vendors (AWS, GCP, Azure) and object storage.

- Expertise in distributed caching, reliability and performance engineering.

- Proven ability to set technical direction across multiple teams or divisions and influence executive decisions.
